item.title: VAGEN framework introduced for training multi-turn vision-language model agents
item.description:
VAGEN framework introduced for training multi-turn vision-language model agents

VAGEN is a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework specifically designed for training multi-turn vision-language model (VLM) agents. The framework enables these agents to build an internal world model through explicit visual state reasoning.

🔍 Overview

  • VAGEN functions as a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework built for VLM agents.
  • It supports a novel approach called World Modeling RL, which improves multi-turn performance by explicitly supervising the world model reasoning process.
  • The framework frames multi-turn VLM agentic tasks as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP).

🧩 How it works

  • World Modeling RL: A reinforcement learning approach that supervises the world model reasoning process to enhance agent performance.
  • StateEstimation: A reinforcement signal that helps the agent determine “what is the current state?”
  • TransitionModeling: A reinforcement signal that helps the agent determine “what comes next?”
  • LLM-as-Judge: Used to provide a world-modeling reward for the StateEstimation and TransitionModeling signals.
  • Architecture Decoupling: The reusable harness, environment, model, rollout, and evaluation boundaries keep world-modeling signals independent from the selected training algorithm.

⚙️ Key details

  • VAGEN-Lite: A lightweight and clean reimplementation of VAGEN built on the VERL agent-loop for easy customization and stable performance.
  • Version Support: Added support for Verl 0.9.0, which decoupled the environment and harness layer.
  • Legacy Code: Previous full-featured releases are available on the vagen-legacy branch, and the last commit before major updates is tagged as vagen-lite-verl-v0.6.1-final.

🚀 Availability

  • VAGEN-Lite Release: Introducing VAGEN-Lite in December 2025 as a lightweight reimplementation.
  • Branch Migration: The main branch migrated to VAGEN-Lite in February 2026.
  • Verl Update: Support for Verl 0.9.0 added in August 2026, marking a major update that decoupled the environment and harness layer.

#VAGEN #RL #VLM #AI #Agents #ReinforcementLearning

item.title: Mastra AI releases skills framework for building AI applications with TypeScript
item.description:
Mastra AI releases skills framework for building AI applications with TypeScript

Mastra is a framework for building AI-powered applications and agents with a modern TypeScript stack. It supports skill discovery via the .well-known standard and provides installation methods through npx skills add https://mastra.ai/.

🔍 Overview

Mastra introduces a skills framework for developing AI applications using TypeScript. The system enables automatic skill discovery through the .well-known skills standard, allowing developers to discover capabilities without manual configuration.

🧩 How it works

The framework implements progressive disclosure with reference files covering multiple development aspects:

Reference File Purpose
create-mastra.md Setup & Installation
embedded-docs.md Find APIs in node_modules/@mastra/*/dist/docs/
remote-docs.md Fetch from https://mastra.ai/llms.txt
common-errors.md Common errors and solutions
migration-guide.md Version upgrade workflows
mastra-api.md Inspect and call resources on local, platform, or remote servers
platform.md Build and deploy apps to Mastra Platform
gateway.md One key for many providers, failover, spend tracking
trace-query.md Select completed traces with recursive predicates
feedback.md Report verified bugs and concrete documentation defects

The main skill file teaches core concepts and routes to appropriate reference files based on user questions. A standalone Factory skill enables coding agents using mastra api factory, covering first-use CLI/login checks and URL-based connection capabilities.

⚙️ Key details

Installation Methods

  • npx skills add mastra-ai/skills
  • gh skill install mastra-ai/skills
  • git clone https://github.com/mastra-ai/skills.git (then configure agent to load from cloned directory)

Well-Known Discovery

  • RFC 8615 Well-Known URI: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/
  • Index: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/index.json
  • Mastra skill: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/mastra/SKILL.md
  • Factory skill: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/mastra-factory/SKILL.md

Factory Skill Features

The Factory skill is a comprehensive skill for AI development that covers:

  • First-use CLI/login checks
  • URL-based connection from any directory
  • Project and queue summaries
  • Work-item session/thread and memory inspection
  • Health interpretation
  • User-authorized operations

Installation Options

  • npx skills add mastra-ai/skills --skill mastra-factory (install just the Factory skill with interactive agent/scope selection)
  • Global install with --agent <agent> -g for supported agents explicitly
  • Multi-agent installs can partially succeed; verify with npx skills list (add -g for global scope)

🚀 Availability

The skills repository is available via:

  • GitHub: git clone https://github.com/mastra-ai/skills.git
  • RFC 8615 Well-Known URI for automatic discovery
  • Direct URL installation: npx skills add https://mastra.ai/

The repository is served via Apache-2.0 license and welcomes contributions through forking, improvement to SKILL.md files, testing with development workflows, and submitting pull requests.

#TypeScript #AI #framework #skills #agents #development

Source: mastra-ai/skills

item.title: Introducing the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework for AI Agents
item.description:
Introducing the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework for AI Agents

The Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF) has been released as a framework-agnostic evaluation system for AI agents, allowing users to invoke any agent and score it on multiple metrics.

🔍 Overview

UAEF can be plugged into any agentic platform to measure agent quality across 36 built-in metrics, persist results to AWS, and track performance over time.

⚙️ Key details

  • Works with LangGraph, LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Langfuse, Strands, AgentCore, or any custom framework via adapters.
  • One evaluate() call gives scores across tool calling, response quality, safety, performance, reasoning, and more.
  • Track experiments against baselines, catch regressions automatically, and get LLM-generated insights.
  • Uses uv for dependency management, with pyproject.toml and uv.lock as the single source of truth for all dependencies.

🚀 Availability

  • Use UAEF as a Python library
  • Deploy the service to AWS
  • Run the demo app locally
  • Clone via git clone https://github.com/awslabs/uaef.git
  • Install dependencies using uv sync or install from a wheel file using uv pip install ./packages/uaef-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl

#AI #Agents #Evaluation #AWS #Python

Source: awslabs/uaef

item.title: Hugging Face introduces RL-trained harness adapters for improved LLM efficiency
item.description:
Hugging Face introduces RL-trained harness adapters for improved LLM efficiency

Hugging Face has introduced “harness adapters,” a method for adapting favorite models to specific agent harnesses using reinforcement learning (RL) to improve performance and cost efficiency. While base models generally target general performance, combining a model with a specific harness often leaves performance and efficiency on the table for targeted tasks. By training custom adapters on specific task distributions, developers can squeeze more capability out of existing models for their specific use cases.

🧩 How it works

The technique involves combining RL on a custom task distribution with the user’s favorite agent harness. This process yields more accurate and efficient models specifically for that target harness and task combination. The core mechanism is that models are not fully optimized for every harness and task; they are optimized for general performance. With RL, a custom harness adapter can be trained to optimize the model for the specific harness and task at hand.

In recent experiments, researchers froze the weights of the Qwen3.8-27B model and added a custom RL-trained LoRA adapter. This approach resulted in the model reasoning less, calling fewer tools, and performing better on the first attempt.

Model / Configuration Terminal-Bench 2.1 Score Avg Tokens per Task
Qwen3.8-27B (Base) 39% 2.9K
Qwen3.8-27B (with RL LoRA) 55% 1.5K

⚙️ Key details

To validate this approach on harder real-world software engineering tasks, the team trained one LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B for each of three agent harnesses: Pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenCode. The RL training occurred inside the harness itself. Datasets, training, and agent rollouts were managed on the Hub in Jobs using TRL’s AsyncGRPOTrainer, OpenEnv, and harbor.

Key technical components of the recipe include:

  • Super Adapter: The three individual LoRAs were merged into a single “super adapter” that runs unchanged under all three harnesses.
  • Docker Images: Ready-to-use docker images for RL tasks are provided with target harnesses pre-installed. The final images use Pi 1.5.2, OpenCode 2.2.7, and Hermes Agent v0.22.6.
  • Custom Dataset Pipeline: A custom dataset for agentic coding was created using the Hub, OpenEnv, and Repo2RLEnv. This pipeline combines task retrieval from existing RL environments, task generation via Repo2RLEnv, and task validation with OpenEnv.
  • Task Sources:
    • SWE-smith injects bugs into real Python and Go repositories using LLM rewrites or mutations.
    • SWE-Gym (packaged as Harbor tasks in TaskTrove) converts real GitHub issues and merged fixes into tasks.
    • Tasksmith generates tasks from merged pull requests. In one instance, Tasksmith produced 24 valid tasks from 30 merged pull requests in 10 Python repositories.

Every task in the dataset passes an eligibility screen via openenv validate and a difficulty check against the base model. Each harness adapter beat the base model under its own harness on both performance and efficiency benchmarks.

🚀 Availability

All artifacts related to this work, including adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, and the safeagents plugin, are browsable through a Hugging Face collection. A fully reusable recipe is shared so developers can reproduce these results on their own task, harness, and model combinations.

#LLMs #ReinforcementLearning #LoRA #Agents #HuggingFace

Source: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost

item.title: Convex Integrates Mastra for AI Workflow Development
item.description:
Convex Integrates Mastra for AI Workflow Development

Convex has introduced a new integration with Mastra, enabling developers to build and run AI workflows directly on its hosted backend platform. This integration allows users to create agents, define workflows, and execute them asynchronously using Convex serverless functions, while leveraging Convex’s reactivity, storage, and vector capabilities.

🧩 How it Works

The Mastra component for Convex provides full support for durable workflows, including:

  • Asynchronous execution from serverless functions (mutations or actions)
  • Tracking workflow status via reactive queries
  • Resuming workflows after suspension for user input
  • Step forking, joining, and triggering
  • Storage and vector integrations for agent memory and RAG

To use the component, developers must:

  • Have an existing Convex project
  • Install the @convex-dev/mastra package
  • Manually install and export @libsql/client due to bundling issues
  • Call storage.setCtx(ctx) and vector.setCtx(ctx) before using storage or vector features in actions

⚙️ Key Details

The integration enables:

  • Running workflows from both mastra dev and convex dev for rapid iteration
  • Using Convex for agent memory with storage and vector features
  • Supporting agentic workflows involving user input, multiple LLM calls, and third-party integrations
  • Custom mutation steps for transactional operations with guaranteed completion
  • Helper functions to securely export actions for browser usage

#Convex #Mastra #AIWorkflows #Serverless #Agents

Source: convex/mastra

item.title: FastAgency Accelerates Multi‑Agent AI Workflow Deployment
item.description:
FastAgency Accelerates Multi‑Agent AI Workflow Deployment

🔍 Overview

  • FastAgency is an open‑source framework that provides a unified programming interface for deploying agentic workflows written in AG2 (formerly AutoGen).
  • It is designed to accelerate the transition from prototype to production for multi‑agent AI workflows.

🧩 How it Works

  • With only a few lines of code, developers can create web chat applications or REST API services that interact with agents of their choice.
  • The same underlying workflows can be deployed to console‑based applications via ConsoleUI or web‑based applications via MesopUI without rewriting code.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Multi‑framework support and powerful API integration capabilities streamline deployment, saving time and effort while maintaining flexibility and performance.
  • FastAgency enables seamless scaling of Jupyter notebook prototypes into fully functional, production‑ready applications.
  • A fully distributed system can be deployed using internal message brokers coordinating multiple machines in multiple datacenters by changing only a few lines of code from the local development setup.

📡 API Integration

  • Integrating external APIs into agent workflows is straightforward: import an OpenAPI specification with a single line of code and connect it to agents with another line.
  • Example: a weather API can be integrated to provide dynamic real‑time weather updates to users.

🧪 Testing & Reliability

  • FastAgency provides a Tester Class that lets developers write and execute tests for multi‑agent workflows.
  • The Tester Class integrates with CI pipelines, allowing early bug detection and ensuring workflows remain functional as they scale.

🚀 Availability

  • FastAgency is an open‑source project that claims to be the fastest way to bring multi‑agent workflows to production.

item.title: VHD-Play Improves Qwen3.6 Agentic Performance
item.description:
VHD-Play Improves Qwen3.6 Agentic Performance

VHD-Play is an update to an AI development that improves agentic capabilities by generating environments and training a model to solve them.

🔍 Overview

VHD-Play reverses a dependency by sampling and solving a mathematical model before a corpus-grounded setter renders its decision process as stateful tools. The executable dynamics and trajectory-scoring reference are inherited from the same solved model.

⚙️ Key details

  • The pipeline produces 3,300 diverse agentic environments at a cost of a few cents each.
  • Training Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on three families raises its mean agentic score from 0.204 to 0.815 in a five-family diagnostic.
  • Gains appear on held-out instances from all three training families and eight unseen mechanism families.
  • Gains extend beyond the generated substrate to external benchmarks for general function calling, travel planning, and 365-day e-commerce.

🧩 How it works

  • A frozen 35B setter realizes larger environments.
  • Scale-matched training retains gains as mechanism size and horizon grow, indicating the potential for an evolving training substrate.
  • The comparison shows that most of the learnable gap lies in stateful interaction rather than underlying problem solving.

📊 Benchmarks

  • On E-Commerce Bench, the trained checkpoint completes every run without bankruptcy and exceeds Qwen3.7-Max.

item.title: iii platform introduces CODER framework for real-time service composition
item.description:
iii platform introduces CODER framework for real-time service composition

iii is a new development platform designed to compose, observe, discover, extend, and react (CODER) to every service in a stack in real time. It unifies backend concerns such as queues, cron, HTTP, state, observability, agents, and sandboxes into a single system surface.

🧩 How it works

iii functions through three core primitives:

  • Workers: Processes that register with the iii engine and define triggers and functions. Examples include TypeScript API services, Python data pipelines, and Rust microservices.
  • Triggers: Declarative events that cause a function to run. These include direct calls, HTTP endpoints, cron schedules, queue subscriptions, state changes, or stream events.
  • Functions: Units of work with a stable identifier that receive input, perform tasks, and return output.

⚙️ Key details

Primitive Description
Worker A registered process that contains functions and triggers
Trigger A declarative event that executes a function
Function A specific unit of work with a stable identifier

When a worker joins the catalog, every other worker is notified and can call it immediately. Developers define workers in a worker-compose.yaml file and deploy them using the iii compose --up command.

💡 Why it matters

This architecture extends to AI agents. When a task requires a capability not currently in the system, an agent can add a worker, discover its functions, and call them using the same interface as a developer. This allows applications and agents to extend the system at runtime.

🚀 Availability

Available workers can be browsed at workers.iii.dev.

#iii #backend #microservices #agents #devops

item.title: Agent Development Kit Updates and SkillNote Registry Introduction
item.description:
Agent Development Kit Updates and SkillNote Registry Introduction

The Agent Development Kit (ADK) has released version 2.0, introducing breaking changes to its agent API, event model, and session schema. Simultaneously, the new open-source SkillNote registry has been introduced to manage skill libraries for AI coding agents.

🛠️ ADK 2.0 Updates

ADK is an open-source, code-first Python toolkit designed for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents. Key updates and features include:

  • Workflow Runtime: A graph-based engine supporting routing, loops, retry logic, state management, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
  • Task API: Facilitates structured agent-to-agent delegation and multi-turn task modes.
  • Compatibility: Sessions from ADK 2.0 are readable by version 1.28+, though incompatible with older 1.x versions.
  • Deployment: Optimized for Gemini but model-agnostic, with options for Cloud Run or Vertex AI Agent Engine.
  • Development: Allows code-first configuration using Agent and Workflow classes, alongside a no-code Agent Config feature.

📋 SkillNote Overview

SkillNote is an open-source, self-hosted registry for managing SKILL.md files used by AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenHands. It addresses description character limits and provides centralized management.

Feature Function
Scope Per-project collections of up to 15 skills
Sync Live browser edits update connected agents within 60 seconds
Feedback Agents rate skills 1-5 with comments
Hosting Self-hosted via Docker and Node.js 20+

🚀 Deployment Details

SkillNote can be initialized using npx skillnote start, which deploys a web, API, and Postgres stack. The system supports:

  • CLI commands: start, stop, restart, status, and logs.
  • Infrastructure: Requires Docker and Node.js 20+; compatible with Podman 4+.
  • Visibility: Web UI accessible at http://localhost:3000 and API at http://localhost:8082.

item.title: Paperclip platform organizes and manages autonomous AI agent workflows
item.description:
Paperclip platform organizes and manages autonomous AI agent workflows

Paperclip is a new platform designed to manage AI agents for business operations, providing a centralized system to organize tasks, goals, budgets, and agent templates instead of managing separate automations.

🧩 How it works

Paperclip allows users to manage business goals by organizing various AI agents—such as those for development, content, marketing, QA, and research—under a single organizational structure. Users can define a company mission, set budgets, and monitor progress via a central dashboard. Agents are hired if they can receive a heartbeat, and they function within an organizational chart that supports automatic delegation of tasks.

⚙️ Key details

  • Agent Management: Supports diverse roles including CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, and marketers across any LLM provider.
  • Operational Workflow: Every task is recorded as a ticket with a clear owner, status, and thread. Instructions, responses, tool calls, and decisions are captured with full tracing.
  • Transparency: The system maintains an append-only history of all activity with no edits or deletions permitted.
  • Context and Integration: Agents use SKILL.md to discover necessary context. The platform is designed for extensibility through drop-in extensions.
  • Financial Tracking: Budgets can be set per agent, task, project, or goal to track costs.

💡 Why it matters

Instead of wiring individual automations from scratch, Paperclip provides a structured environment where agents wake up on a schedule, check their work, and respond to ticket assignments. This approach allows users to manage high-level business goals rather than individual pull requests.

#AI #Automation #Agents #BusinessTools #WorkflowManagement

Source: Paperclip – The app people use to manage AI agents for work

item.title: GLM-4.6: Next-Generation Language Model with Enhanced Capabilities
item.description:
🤖 GLM-4.6: Next-Generation Language Model with Enhanced Capabilities

Advanced language model with 200K context window and superior performance

👋 Join our Discord community. 📖 Check out the GLM-4.6 technical blog, technical report(GLM-4.5), and Zhipu AI technical documentation. 📍 Use GLM-4.6 API services on Z.ai API Platform.👉 One click to GLM-4.6.

🚀 Model Introduction

Compared with GLM-4.5, GLM-4.6 brings several key improvements:

  • Longer context window: The context window has been expanded from 128K to 200K tokens, enabling the model to handle more complex agentic tasks.
  • Superior coding performance: The model achieves higher scores on code benchmarks and demonstrates better real-world performance in applications such as Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code and Kilo Code, including improvements in generating visually polished front-end pages.
  • Advanced reasoning: GLM-4.6 shows a clear improvement in reasoning performance and supports tool use during inference, leading to stronger overall capability.
  • More capable agents: GLM-4.6 exhibits stronger performance in tool using and search-based agents, and integrates more effectively within agent frameworks.
  • Refined writing: Better aligns with human preferences in style and readability, and performs more naturally in role-playing scenarios.

We evaluated GLM-4.6 across eight public benchmarks covering agents, reasoning, and coding. Results show clear gains over GLM-4.5, with GLM-4.6 also holding competitive advantages over leading domestic and international models such as DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus and Claude Sonnet 4.

Performance comparison across multiple benchmarks showcasing GLM-4.6’s superior capabilities

⚙️ Inference

Both GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.6 use the same inference method.

You can check our GitHub repository for more detail.

🔧 Recommended Evaluation Parameters

For general evaluations, we recommend using a sampling temperature of 1.0.

For code-related evaluation tasks (such as LCB), it is further recommended to set:

  • top_p = 0.95
  • top_k = 40

📊 Evaluation

  • For tool-integrated reasoning, please refer to this documentation.
  • For search benchmark, we design a specific format for searching toolcall in thinking mode to support search agent, please refer to this template for the detailed template.

💡 Key Features & Specifications

Feature Specification

Context Window 200K tokens
Tensor Types BF16, F32
Languages English, Chinese

🌟 Model Applications

GLM-4.6 has been integrated into numerous applications and spaces, demonstrating its versatility:

  • 49 Hugging Face Spaces utilizing the model
  • 8 fine-tuned variants available
  • 33 quantized versions for different deployment scenarios

The model excels in various domains including:

  • Text generation and conversational AI
  • Code generation and debugging
  • Agent-based applications
  • Search and reasoning tasks
  • Creative writing and role-playing

🙌 Credits

Originally posted at: https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6

✅ Final Thoughts

GLM-4.6 represents a significant advancement in language model capabilities, offering enhanced context understanding, superior coding performance, and improved reasoning abilities. With its expanded 200K token context window and refined agent capabilities, it positions itself as a competitive solution for complex AI applications. The model’s strong performance across benchmarks, combined with its practical improvements in real-world scenarios, makes it a compelling choice for developers and researchers working on advanced language processing tasks.

item.title: MiniMax-M2: The Future of Efficient AI Coding and Agentic Workflows
item.description:
🚀 MiniMax-M2: The Future of Efficient AI Coding and Agentic Workflows

Redefining efficiency for AI agents with a compact, fast, and cost-effective approach

🌟 Highlights

MiniMax-M2 represents a revolutionary leap in AI model efficiency, delivering Mini size with Max performance for coding and agentic workflows. This compact powerhouse features 230 billion total parameters with only 10 billion active parameters, making it a game-changer for developers seeking sophisticated AI capabilities without the computational overhead.

item.title: GPT-OSS-20B: OpenAI's Open-Weight AI Model for Developers
item.description:
🤖 GPT-OSS-20B: OpenAI’s Open-Weight AI Model for Developers

OpenAI’s breakthrough open-weight model designed for powerful reasoning, agentic tasks, and versatile developer applications

Welcome to the gpt-oss series — OpenAI’s groundbreaking collection of open-weight models engineered for sophisticated reasoning, autonomous agent development, and flexible integration across diverse use cases. This comprehensive guide explores the gpt-oss-20b model, the more compact yet powerful variant in OpenAI’s open-source AI ecosystem.

🚀 Two Flavors of Innovation

OpenAI has strategically released two distinct model variants to address different computational and performance requirements:

| Model | Parameters | Active Parameters | Use Case | Hardware Requirements
gpt-oss-120b 117B 5.1B Production, general purpose, high reasoning Single 80GB GPU
(NVIDIA H100/AMD MI300X)
gpt-oss-20b 21B 3.6B Lower latency, local deployment, specialized tasks 16GB
memory

Both models utilize OpenAI’s proprietary harmony response format and require this specific format for optimal performance and compatibility.

⭐ Key Highlights & Features

🔓 Permissive Apache 2.0 License

Build freely without copyleft restrictions or patent concerns — perfect for experimentation, customization, and commercial deployment scenarios.

⚙️ Configurable Reasoning Effort

Dynamically adjust reasoning intensity across three levels based on your specific requirements and latency constraints:

  • Low: Fast responses for general dialogue
  • Medium: Balanced speed and analytical depth
  • High: Comprehensive and detailed analysis

🔍 Full Chain-of-Thought Access

Gain complete visibility into the model’s reasoning process, enabling easier debugging, validation, and increased confidence in AI-generated outputs. Note: This internal reasoning is designed for developers and not intended for end-user display.

🎯 Fine-Tuning Ready

Fully customize models for your specific domain through comprehensive parameter fine-tuning capabilities.

🤖 Advanced Agentic Capabilities

Leverage native support for:

  • Function Calling with defined schemas
  • Web Browsing using integrated tools
  • Python Code Execution for computational tasks
  • Structured Outputs for consistent data formatting

💾 MXFP4 Quantization

Post-training MXFP4 quantization of MoE (Mixture of Experts) weights enables:

  • gpt-oss-120b: Runs on single 80GB GPU
  • gpt-oss-20b: Operates within 16GB memory footprint
  • All evaluations performed with identical MXFP4 quantization for consistency

🔧 Transformers Integration

Both gpt-oss models integrate seamlessly with Transformers. The chat template automatically applies the harmony response format, or you can implement it manually using the chat template or the openai-harmony package.

Environment Setup:

1

pip install -U transformers kernels torch

from transformers import pipeline import torch

model_id = "openai/gpt-oss-20b" pipe = pipeline(
 "text-generation", model=model_id,
 torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto",
)

messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum mechanics clearly and concisely."},
]

outputs = pipe( messages,
 max_new_tokens=256, )
print(outputs[0]["generated_text"][-1])

OpenAI-Compatible Server:

1

transformers serve transformers chat localhost:8000 --model-name-or-path openai/gpt-oss-20b

🏁 Conclusion

The gpt-oss-20b model represents a significant milestone in democratizing advanced AI capabilities. With its Apache 2.0 license, configurable reasoning levels, and comprehensive tool integration, it empowers developers to build sophisticated AI applications without the constraints typically associated with proprietary models.

Key advantages include its efficient 16GB memory footprint, making it accessible for local deployment, while maintaining robust performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks. The model’s harmony response format ensures consistent behavior, and its fine-tuning capabilities enable domain-specific customization.

Whether you’re developing conversational agents, building autonomous systems, or creating specialized AI applications, gpt-oss-20b provides the foundation for innovative solutions with the transparency and flexibility that open-source development demands.
